Alsa sometimes defaults the sound to some weird values, to solve it, just run alsamixer from a terminal, which should bring up some sort of interface, from there, if you don't immediately see some sort of "bars", press F6 and choose the other option, after you see them, look for the "Master" one, if it has "MM", press the keyboard arrows until it's highlighted and press "m", if it has a number, use the up and down arrows to set the value to something higher.

If this doesn't work, do what @albatrosv13 said and report back, and remember to install "alsa" and "alsautils" (just "apt-cache search alsa" , as I'm not sure what the actual name for the package is) if they are not, even though they are almost for sure.

Edit : the arch wiki has a pretty good article about alsa, even if you're not using arch, most things if not all apply for other distributions as well.

Edit #2 : Explanation : In case you don't know , the channels are the "things" your computer can make sound with, for example, when you run alsamixer, if you have a stereo capable sound system, there will be 2 numbers below each bar separated by <> , the left one corresponds to the left channel and the right one to the right channel, if you up the left value from the master switch for example, you'll notice that the left speaker (or group of speakers in some cases) will be louder than the right one.

For all of those who have switched and are having a hard time finding replacement programs for Office, Photoshop, etc, let's start a list of Linux-friendly, open-source (free) software that can replace proprietary PC software from the get-go! There are commercial options, I'm sure, but I've managed just fine with free software:

  • LibreOffice5 (replaces Microsoft Office) - Ubuntu 15.04 comes with LibreOffice4.x. Remove LibreOffice then install it from the website (LibreOffice5 Direct Download Page, LibreOffice5 Ubuntu Installer).

  • GIMP (Replaces Adobe Photoshop) - Very powerful program, has many of the same features Photoshop does.

  • Steam (native on Linux, replaces Windows version) - Your Windows games will most likely not be available on Linux, though a good number of them are and more are always on the way.

List anything else you'd need a replacement program for and let's see if we can't hook anyone up!

For libreoffice, just add their ppa

Sudo add-apt-repository ppa:libreoffice/ppa

Sudo apt-get update

Then sudo apt-get upgrade if you've already got the older version installed from stock repo or apt-get install libreoffice to get the latest if you haven't already installed it from stock Ubuntu repo.

Then it's always up to date.
